fiction_notice: Fictional simulation. The persona facts come from the official case (page references given). The portfolio, the objective wording, every threshold and every scripted request were invented by the team for the demonstration; the case gives the personas no numbers. Nothing here is advice, a recommendation or a real account.

facts.label: Profile
facts.text: Has a partner and two children; intermediate investment experience.

facts.label: Investment objective
facts.text: He wants balanced capital growth over the medium and long term.

facts.label: Preference
facts.text: Places high importance on environmental, social, and governance (ESG) factors.

facts.label: Constraint
facts.text: Wants to avoid companies involved in significant environmental or social controversies.

facts.label: Preference
facts.text: Seeks a balance between growth potential and stability.

what_this_persona_tests.text: Can the system incorporate more than return and risk? It should consider financial factors and personal preferences, rather than selecting solely for potential return.

objectives.original_words: Balanced growth over 8 to 12 years; ESG matters to me; I want to avoid oil and companies involved in significant controversies.

scenario_rules.original_words: Fictional scenario: by 'oil' I mean no holdings labelled Energy in what my funds report.
scenario_rules.scope_description: Maximum total equity exposure to holdings labelled 'Energy': the sector label reported in the fund issuer's holdings file for fund constituents, the instrument registry label for direct holdings. Constituents without a label count as unknown, not as zero. A sector label is not a list of oil producers and is not a controversy finding. Bond funds, commodity funds and crypto assets are outside this rule's scope and are not assessed.

scenario_rules.original_words: Fictional scenario: no companies with a regulatory finding, court ruling or settlement in the registry.
scenario_rules.scope_description: Maximum total equity exposure to companies with a controversy-registry record of nature REGULATORY_FINDING, COURT_RULING, SETTLEMENT. Companies without a record are not assessed: absence from the registry is unknown, never a pass. Bond funds, commodity funds and crypto assets are outside this rule's scope and are not assessed.

demo_phrases.original_words: Balanced growth over 8 to 12 years; ESG matters to me; I want to avoid oil and companies involved in significant controversies.
demo_phrases.note: 'oil' is ambiguous: named companies, oil producers, fossil fuels or the Energy sector label. The interpreter must ask, offer the supported definitions and mark the others unsupported. The avoidance of oil is our scenario wording; the case itself only mentions controversies (Case p.6).

demo_requests.label: Make SPY 15% of the portfolio (final direct weight), funded from cash

purchase_request.original_words: Buy SPY so that it is 15% of my portfolio.

demo_challenge.label: Mateo clarifies what he meant by oil

payload.text: By oil I meant companies that produce oil, not pipelines or utilities.

demo_steps.description: Load Mateo and his fictional portfolio (25% cash, 25% XBB.TO, 20% XIU.TO, 15% ESGV, 5% MSFT, 5% CNR.TO, 5% FTS.TO).

Interpret his sentence: the interpreter asks what 'oil' means. Mateo picks the Energy sector label as reported by funds and sets the tolerated exposure to 0; the controversy exclusion is confirmed separately.
Request SPY at a final direct weight of 0.15, funded from cash.
The investigation looks up holdings, sector labels and the controversy registry; no 2022 replay because no scenario rule exists.

Both rules are already breached by the starting portfolio through XIU.TO: two findings about the starting portfolio, kept apart from the effect of the purchase. The controversy rule fails on dated registry records (Enbridge and Canadian Natural Resources before the purchase; Exxon Mobil is added by SPY); every company without a record stays 'not assessed', never 'clean'. What SPY adds to the Energy exclusion is shown as unresolved, because the SPY holdings file has no sector labels. ESGV is unknown because its holdings were not acquired.
Mateo clarifies his preference; the reply is a new draft interpretation, with 'oil producers' reported as an unsupported definition.
